1.title: Comfort in Affliction
1.themes: Comfort, Suffering, Sincerity, Reliability of God
1.outline:
I. Salutation (1:1-2)
II. The God of All Comfort (1:3-11)
III. Paul's Change of Plans (1:12-24)
1.summary: Paul opens his letter by praising God as the source of all comfort, who comforts believers in their afflictions so they can comfort others. He explains his recent severe suffering in Asia. He then defends his integrity and sincerity, clarifying why he had to alter his travel plans to visit Corinth, assuring them that God's promises in Christ are always 'Yes.'

2.title: Forgiveness and the Aroma of Christ
2.outline:
I. A Painful Visit Avoided (2:1-4)
II. Forgiveness for the Offender (2:5-11)
III. Ministry in Troas and Macedonia (2:12-13)
IV. Triumphant Ministry (2:14-17)
2.summary: Paul explains he wrote his previous 'severe letter' out of deep love, not to cause pain. He urges the Corinthians to forgive and comfort the person who had caused grief, lest Satan outwit them. Paul describes his anxiety waiting for Titus and rejoices that God always leads believers in triumph in Christ, making them the pleasing aroma of Christ to God.

3.title: Ministers of the New Covenant
3.themes: New Covenant, The Spirit vs. The Letter, Glory of the Gospel
3.outline:
I. Letters of Recommendation (3:1-3)
II. The Glory of the New Covenant (3:4-11)
III. The Veil Removed (3:12-18)
3.summary: Paul asserts that he doesn't need letters of recommendation because the Corinthians themselves are his letter, written by the Spirit on human hearts. He contrasts the glory of the old covenant of the law, which is fading, with the surpassing glory of the new covenant of the Spirit. With unveiled faces, believers are transformed into the Lord's image.

4.title: Treasure in Jars of Clay
4.themes: Perseverance, Light of the Gospel, Earthly Frailty, Eternal Glory
4.outline:
I. The Light of the Gospel (4:1-6)
II. Treasure in Jars of Clay (4:7-12)
III. Living by Faith (4:13-18)
4.summary: Paul proclaims the light of the gospel, noting that Satan has blinded the minds of unbelievers. He describes believers as fragile 'jars of clay' holding the treasure of the gospel, showing that this all-surpassing power is from God. Despite facing severe hardships, Paul doesn't lose heart, knowing that temporary troubles achieve an eternal glory.

5.title: The Ministry of Reconciliation
5.themes: Heavenly Dwelling, Judgment, New Creation, Reconciliation
5.outline:
I. Our Heavenly Dwelling (5:1-10)
II. The Ministry of Reconciliation (5:11-21)
5.summary: Paul anticipates the eternal, heavenly body that awaits believers, groaning for this heavenly dwelling. He reminds them of the judgment seat of Christ. He explains that knowing the fear of the Lord drives his ministry, declaring that anyone in Christ is a new creation. God has given believers the ministry of reconciliation, calling them to be Christ's ambassadors.

6.title: Hardships and Purity
6.themes: Endurance in Ministry, Unequal Yokes, Holiness
6.outline:
I. Paul's Hardships in Ministry (6:1-13)
II. Warning Against Yoking with Unbelievers (6:14-18)
6.summary: Paul describes the intense hardships and trials he and his companions have endured as servants of God, pleading with the Corinthians to open their hearts wide. He follows this with a strong exhortation not to be unequally yoked with unbelievers, urging them to separate from impurity so that God may dwell among them.

7.title: Joy in Repentance
7.outline:
I. Exhortation to Holiness (7:1)
II. Paul's Joy over the Corinthians' Repentance (7:2-16)
7.summary: Concluding his plea for purity, Paul asks the Corinthians to make room for him in their hearts. He expresses his profound joy at the arrival of Titus, who brought news of their longing, deep sorrow, and zeal for Paul. He contrasts godly sorrow, which brings repentance and salvation, with worldly sorrow, celebrating their renewed relationship.

8.title: The Grace of Giving
8.themes: Generosity, Collection for the Saints, Equality
8.outline:
I. The Generosity of the Macedonians (8:1-7)
II. Christ's Example of Grace (8:8-15)
III. Titus Sent to Receive the Collection (8:16-24)
8.summary: Paul urges the Corinthians to excel in the grace of giving, citing the extreme generosity of the Macedonian churches despite their poverty. He points to the example of Christ, who became poor so that others might become rich. Paul commends Titus and other brothers who are coming to Corinth to help administer the collection for the saints.

9.title: God Loves a Cheerful Giver
9.themes: Sowing and Reaping, Cheerful Giving, Thanksgiving
9.outline:
I. Readiness to Give (9:1-5)
II. Bountiful Sowing and Reaping (9:6-15)
9.summary: Paul continues his discussion on the collection for the saints in Jerusalem, praising the Corinthians' initial eagerness. He uses the principle of sowing and reaping to encourage them to give generously and cheerfully, not under compulsion. He assures them that God will abundantly provide for them and that their generosity will result in thanksgiving to God.

10.title: Paul's Defense of His Ministry
10.themes: Spiritual Warfare, Apostolic Authority, Boasting in the Lord
10.outline:
I. Paul Defends His Authority (10:1-11)
II. Proper Boasting (10:12-18)
10.summary: Paul shifts his tone, defending his apostolic authority against critics who say his letters are weighty but his presence is weak. He explains that his weapons are not worldly but have divine power to demolish strongholds. He criticizes those who commend themselves by comparing themselves to others, asserting that any boasting should only be in the Lord.

11.title: Paul and the False Apostles
11.themes: Godly Jealousy, False Apostles, Suffering for Christ
11.outline:
I. Paul's Godly Jealousy (11:1-6)
II. Paul's Support in Ministry (11:7-15)
III. Paul's Sufferings as an Apostle (11:16-33)
11.summary: Paul expresses a 'godly jealousy' for the Corinthians, fearing they are being led astray by 'super-apostles' preaching a different Jesus. He exposes these false apostles as deceitful workers masquerading as servants of righteousness. He then reluctantly 'boasts' in his weaknesses, cataloging his extensive sufferings, beatings, shipwrecks, and daily anxieties for the churches.

12.title: Paul's Vision and Thorn in the Flesh
12.themes: Visions, Weakness, Grace, Concern for the Corinthian Church
12.outline:
I. Paul's Vision of Paradise (12:1-6)
II. The Thorn in the Flesh (12:7-10)
III. Paul's Concern for the Corinthians (12:11-21)
12.summary: Paul describes a vision where he was caught up to the third heaven. To keep him from becoming conceited, he was given a 'thorn in the flesh.' Despite pleading for its removal, God answered, 'My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.' Paul expresses concern that upon his next visit, he may find them unrepentant of sin.

13.title: Final Warnings and Greetings
13.themes: Self-Examination, Restoration, Apostolic Authority, Trinitarian Blessing
13.outline:
I. Final Warnings (13:1-4)
II. Call to Self-Examination (13:5-10)
III. Final Greetings and Benediction (13:11-14)
13.summary: Preparing for his third visit, Paul warns that he will not spare those who have sinned. He urges the Corinthians to examine themselves to see whether they are in the faith. He expresses his hope that they will do what is right. He concludes the letter with final exhortations to strive for full restoration and offers a beautiful Trinitarian benediction.
